records.summary: Twenty of the 24 fields come from Honda's own 2024 newsroom spec sheet, pricing release, consumer site and 2022 launch material (engine, 158 hp / 138 lb-ft, CVT, FWD, 2,877-lb LX curb weight, suspension, brakes, MSRP, warranty) plus EPA fueleconomy.gov for 31/40/35 mpg, with Edmunds corroborating the key numbers; everything was read from search-result summaries because pages could not be opened. Two fields rest on aggregator or secondary sites alone and are the weakest entries: ground clearance (5.3 in from CarEdge, with other aggregators saying 4.8 and 4.4 in) and unibody construction (Auto123's wording, no Honda document found). The only measured 0-60 (9.7 s, Consumer Reports) is from a Civic Sport with the same 2.0L/CVT powertrain rather than an LX and has no second test behind it, and no manufacturer or instrumented top speed, skidpad or braking figure for an LX-spec car was found (the Car and Driver and MotorTrend sedan tests that surfaced were of the 1.5-turbo Touring), so those five fields are listed as not found; MPGe, EV range and production units do not apply to this car.

conflicts.values: 2.9 s (Nissan's claim with launch control, per Motor1's 2020 NISMO review; MotorTrend measured 2.9 s on 2015 and 2017 NISMOs, per GT-R Life forum reposts; 0-60specs and FastestLaps list a Car and Driver 2.9 s for the 2015 NISMO) vs 3.3 s (MotorWeek's own test of a 2020 NISMO, https://motorweek.org/road_tests/2020-nissan-gt-r-nismo/) vs 2.48 s (TopSpeed's 2020 'Driven' review, public-road run with no stated method; repeated by a Wikipedia list) vs spec-site estimates from 2.4 to 3.3 s

MotorWeek's 3.3 s is the only measured result found on a publisher's own page for a 2020-on NISMO; use it instead if a strictly first-hand measured figure is required. No 2024-model-year test could be reached.

conflicts.resolution: Used 196 mph because it is the only figure explicitly attributed to the manufacturer. Nissan USA publishes no top speed for the 2024 car, so this is a Europe-market claim for the same 600 PS NISMO, not a US or 2024-specific number.

records.summary: 22 of 26 fields come from Nissan's own 2024 press kit and warranty booklet or from EPA fueleconomy.gov (all read from search-result summaries, since pages could not be opened); the other 4 (0-60, top speed, skidpad grip and 60-0 braking) rest on aggregator-class third-party relays, because Car and Driver, MotorTrend and Road & Track are blocked to the search tool and the web-search budget ran out before any 2020-2024 NISMO instrumented test could be reached. Weakest: grip and braking are MotorTrend numbers for a 2017 NISMO with steel brakes quoted on a forum, top speed is Nissan's European 196 mph claim relayed by evo (US outlets quote an unattributed 205 mph), and 0-60 is Nissan's 2.9 s claim relayed by Motor1 (MotorWeek itself measured 3.3 s on a 2020 NISMO). Not sourced: whether top speed is governed, 70-0 braking, a US ground clearance (Nissan Japan's spec sheet lists 110 mm for the JDM NISMO, left unconverted under the no-conversion rule) and any official build count; the EV fields do not apply.

fields.note: The 2024 release describes a fifth-generation hybrid system pairing a 2.0L inline-four with two motor-generators through a planetary-type CVT. The engine code M20A-FXS appears in Toyota pressroom text; the code and the words 'Atkinson cycle' are also in Toyota's 2023 Prius Product Information sheet (corroborating link, a copy hosted on PriusChat, previous model year of the same generation). Read from search-result excerpts, not from the opened page.

Non-plug-in gasoline-electric hybrid (Cars.com: 'Gas/Electric Hybrid'); the EPA rates it on regular gasoline. The plug-in car is the separate Prius Prime.

Net combined hybrid system output for front-wheel-drive models; Toyota quotes 196 net hp with e-AWD. Automotive Fleet (trade press restating Toyota's announcement) and Edmunds (194 hp @ 6,000 rpm for the LE) give the same figure. KBB and CarsDirect list 150 hp, which is the gasoline engine alone; one Cars.com LE page shows 196 hp.

CAVEAT: this is not a combined system torque. Toyota's 2024 release headline reads 'Powerful Hybrid System with up to 196-hp and 152 lb.-ft. of torque' and does not say which component the 152 lb-ft describes; AutoInformed attributes 152 lb-ft to the front-drive motor-generator. Aggregators (Cars.com, AutoPadre, Auto123, KBB, CarsDirect) list 139 lb-ft @ 4,400 rpm, which is the gasoline engine alone. Toyota publishes no total system torque in the results found.

conflicts.values: $27,650 (Toyota newsroom launch release of October 10, 2023, excluding dealer processing and handling; toyota.com snippet) vs $27,950 (MSRP shown on the EPA fueleconomy.gov listing); Car and Driver's syndicated Prius comparison quotes a $29,045 starting price without the excerpt saying what it includes
conflicts.resolution: $27,650 recorded as Toyota's published launch MSRP. The higher figures may reflect a later in-year price or the inclusion of delivery charges; this could not be checked because the search budget ran out.

conflicts.values: 171 ft (Car and Driver test of a 2023 Prius Limited FWD on 19-inch tires, via https://autos.yahoo.com/tested-2023-toyota-prius-drives-120000770.html) vs 194 ft (search excerpts of Car and Driver's Prius vs Prius Prime comparison, https://autos.yahoo.com/toyota-prius-prius-prime-hybrids-140000505.html) vs 174 ft (a repost of that comparison on invoice-pricing.com)
conflicts.resolution: Not recorded. The tested car was a Limited on 19-inch tires, not an LE on 17-inch tires, and the excerpts disagree with each other. The same comparison gives 0.87 g on the skidpad for that Limited, also not recorded.

conflicts.values: 112 mph (unattributed figure in an excerpt of a 2023 Prius Limited review) vs 132 mph and 122 mph (Motor Matchup simulated estimates for 2023 Limited variants)
conflicts.resolution: Not recorded. No manufacturer figure and no instrumented-test top speed was surfaced, so whether the car is speed-limited is also unsourced.

records.summary: Every value was read from web-search result summaries (pages could not be opened), and the shared search budget ran out before top speed, a 2024 Toyota spec sheet, rear brakes and the MSRP discrepancy could be chased. Of 21 recorded fields, 14 trace to Toyota's own material (13 to the 2024 Prius newsroom release, front brakes to Toyota's 2023 product-information sheet found as a copy on PriusChat), 3 to EPA fueleconomy.gov, and 4 rest on aggregator sites as primary source: curb weight (KBB/Edmunds 3,097 lb, matched by Toyota's 2023 LE figure), ground clearance (KBB/Edmunds), and front and rear suspension type (Auto123/Cars.com pages for the 2023 car, another configuration). Weakest points: torque (Toyota's headline 152 lb-ft is apparently the front motor's figure, while aggregators list 139 lb-ft for the engine alone, and no system torque is published); the MSRP ($27,650 at launch vs $27,950 on fueleconomy.gov); no top speed at all; no skidpad or braking figure, because the only instrumented test found was Car and Driver's 2023 Limited FWD on 19-inch tires, left out as a different trim; and aspiration, construction and rear brakes, which no result stated in words (Toyota's text names a 2.0L Atkinson-cycle four and the TNGA-C platform only).
